title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous pages. A group U acts on a space P with quotient T = P/U. E is a set of base points with a map i_E : E -> P, and a group mu acts on E compatibly with i_E through a homomorphism (6), presumably mu -> U. The quotient E_0 = E/mu maps to T. C' is the groupoid on E induced from Pi_1(P), and C is the groupoid on E_0 induced from Pi_1(T). The functor f : C' -> C makes the square (11) commute, and its horizontal arrows are equivalences when E -> Pi_0 is surjective. Transport of structure makes mu act on C' and Pi_1(P), and trivially on C and Pi_1(T).

This page relates that mu-action to the internal pi-structure (pi acting through automorphisms of the identity functor). Take the extension 0 -> pi -> U~ -> U -> 0 (12). Pull it back along mu -> U to get 0 -> pi -> calE -> mu -> 0 (13), assumed commutative (central at least).

Let x, y be two objects of E in the same fibre C'_xi of f over xi in E_0, i.e. congruent mod mu. Assume mu acts freely on E; the note says this is automatic if i_E is injective. Then y = z.x for a unique z = y - x in mu. Claim (14): there is a canonical isomorphism of pi-torsors Isom_{C'_xi}(x,y) = calE_{y-x}, where calE_z is the fibre of calE over z. This is compatible with composition in C'_xi, which corresponds to addition in calE.

So the fibre groupoid C'_xi is the groupoid built from the central extension restricted to the mu-torsor calE_xi. Its objects are the points of that torsor, and the arrows x -> y form the fibre of calE over y - x. This is (15) on the next page, C'_xi = calE(calE_xi). It feeds the general definition there of a strict (pi,mu)-fibration of groupoids subordinate to a central extension.

Purpose in the Teichmüller programme: describe how an extension, for instance a central Z-extension of a mapping class group, restricts to a finite automorphism group mu of a point. The output is the local stacky structure of the Teichmüller groupoids at special points, in the style of tangential base points.
errors: Not an error, but a gap: canonicity of (14) presupposes that U~ acts on Pi_1(P) lifting the U-action (the pi-structure), which is only implicit on this page.

For compatibility with composition written additively, calE must be commutative, or at least the order of composition must be fixed. Grothendieck flags this with 'ext. commutative'; otherwise one needs Isom(y,w) x Isom(x,y) -> Isom(x,w) to match multiplication calE_{w-y} x calE_{y-x} -> calE_{w-x} in the right order.
Freeness of the mu-action on the fibre is needed for y-x to be well defined; it is stated as a hypothesis.

ideas.what: Fibre of the induced groupoid functor C' -> C identified with the groupoid of a central extension of mu by pi, restricted to a mu-torsor (Isom(x,y) = fibre of the extension over y-x)
ideas.modern_name: Groupoid/gerbe associated to a central extension; banded (pi-)gerbe over a torsor; 2-group actions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Giraud's non-abelian cohomology / gerbes; Brown on groupoids)

ideas.what: Pulling back a central extension of the mapping-class-type group U along a finite subgroup mu (automorphisms of a point) to control the local groupoid structure
ideas.modern_name: Restriction of central extensions to stabilizers; orbifold/stacky points of moduli stacks
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in the theory of mapping class groups and moduli stacks
ideas.where_published: Related remarks in Esquisse d'un programme

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard lemma: the fibre groupoid is the groupoid of a pulled-back central extension. It sets up the notion of a (pi,mu)-fibration of groupoids on the next page, but nothing on this page goes beyond known gerbe/extension yoga.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'opère trivialement sur C et sur Pi_1(T).'
'Soient x, y deux points de E [not calE] qui soient dans une même fibre C'_xi de C' sur C'.
'Conchoïdique [?] ni [?] i.e. injectif' is probably 'Condition automatique si i_E injectif'.
'avec les Pi-structures sur xi Pi_1(xi), ou celle de f' is probably 'avec la Pi-structure sur Pi_1(P), ou celle de C' qui s'en déduit par transport de structure'.
The subscript in (14) is Isom_{C'_xi}(x,y) = calE_{y-x}.
